subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should this be fixed by preserving parallel distinct ACP child sessions and repairing ACPX/Claude launch readiness, or by introducing a deliberate ACP concurrency gate for this backend/workflow?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally allow distinct ACP sessions to run in parallel, so automation should not add broad serialization without maintainer direction and live reproduction evidence.

options.title: Preserve parallelism and fix launch readiness
options.body: Keep distinct ACP sessions parallel by default, reproduce the two-spawn failure live, and repair the confirmed ACPX/OpenClaw startup boundary.

options.title: Add an explicit ACP concurrency gate
options.body: Introduce a deliberate backend/session concurrency gate only if maintainers decide ACPX/Claude cannot safely support rapid parallel starts.

options.title: Defer pending fresh evidence
options.body: Keep the issue in needs-info/manual-review until a current live ACPX/Claude reproduction identifies the failing boundary.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism and fix launch readiness
recommendation.body: Keep distinct ACP sessions parallel by default, reproduce the two-spawn failure live, and repair the confirmed ACPX/OpenClaw startup boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for ACP spawn/control-plane and ACPX integration points to osolmaz's merged feature and runtime refactor work.
